# CogPO dimension mapping

[CogPO](http://www.cogpo.org/) describes an experimental condition along three
dimensions with closed vocabularies: the stimulus (its modality, kind and role), the
response (the body part and the kind of overt act) and the instructions. The Catalog
adopts these six vocabularies as the starting point for its task **facets**, the
attributes a dataset search can filter on, and pairs each value with the
[HED schema](https://www.hedtags.org/) tag that expresses it, so that a facet value on
a task can become a tag on the dataset's events.

This page lists every value: where it came from, what it means, and which HED 8.4.0 tag
carries it. The source of record is `data/facet_defs.tsv`. Filling the facets on the
task records is separate work and has not started; this page is the vocabulary, not the
assignments.

## How the vocabulary was built

Each CogPO value was kept with its CogPO definition and identifier, and given the HED
8.4.0 tag or tags that express it. Where HED has the same concept under the same or an
equivalent name the note says "Exact tag"; where it has only a parent or a neighbour the
note names it; where it has nothing the tag column is empty and the note says why.

Two kinds of value were added. **From HED**: roles and instructions that HED has, CogPO
lacks and the Catalog's tasks need, such as the distractor, cue, oddball, stop-signal and
prime roles and the judge, recognize, predict, plan and switch-attention instructions.
**By the Catalog**: values neither resource has and the tasks need, such as monetary
amounts and playing cards as stimuli, rating as a response, and choose, withhold and
navigate as instructions. Every row's `source` column says which.

Nothing was dropped from the vocabularies. The CogPO values that are out of the
Catalog's scope, acupuncture, TMS, infusion, micturition, stay in the tables so that the
correspondence is complete; no Catalog task will carry them.

## Stimulus modality

CogPO's six modalities map one to one onto HED's `Sensory-presentation` tags, and its
four tactile subtypes onto a presentation tag plus a `Tactile-attribute` or
`Somatic-attribute`. The one gap is interoception, which HED 8.4.0 does not name.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_stimulus_modality.md
```

## Stimulus kind

CogPO's 41 explicit stimuli are the widest vocabulary and the one where HED's coverage
is most uneven. Language items (`Word`, `Pseudoword`, `Syllable`, `Character`), sounds
(`Tone`, `Click`, `Signal-noise`, `Musical-sound`, `Vocalized-sound`), faces, images and
geometric objects (`Dots`, `Pattern`, `2D-shape`) are all present. HED has no item for
a digit or a number, for food, an odor or a puff of air, for speech as a stimulus, or
for the physiological stimuli (electrical, thermal, laser, infusion, TMS). Note also that
HED's `Letter` is a piece of correspondence, so an alphabetic letter is a `Character`.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_stimulus_kind.md
```

## Stimulus role

CogPO's four roles exist only on its wiki; the OWL class has no members. All four are
HED tags. HED's `Task-stimulus-role` vocabulary is much richer, and the Catalog takes
eight more values from it.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_stimulus_role.md
```

## Response modality

CogPO's body parts are Foundational Model of Anatomy classes with no label in the OWL;
the labels here were checked against the FMA through the EBI Ontology Lookup Service.
HED's `Body-part` subtree has every one except arm and leg, for which the parent
`Upper-extremity` or `Lower-extremity` stands in.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_response_modality.md
```

## Response kind

HED's `Action` subtree covers the common responses directly (`Press`, `Saccade`,
`Blink`, `Speak`, `Point`, `Grasp`, `Write`, `Swallow`, `Hold-breath`, `Smile`,
`Whistle`). A button press is two tags, the action `Press` and the device pressed
(`Push-button`, `Keyboard-key` or `Mouse-button`), which is why the Catalog splits
CogPO's single Button Press into three device-specific values. HED has no tap, draw or
drink action, and a rating is a `Participant-response` carrying a value rather than an
action of its own.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_response_kind.md
```

## Instructions

CogPO's instruction verbs are almost all HED `Think` or `Perform` actions
(`Attend-to`, `Count`, `Detect`, `Discriminate`, `Encode`, `Generate`, `Imagine`,
`Recall`, `Track`, `Read`, `Repeat`, `Rest`). Name is the exception: HED has `Identify`
for the judgement and `Speak` for the response but no naming action. HED's `Think`
vocabulary is larger than CogPO's and supplies eight instructions the Catalog's tasks
need; five more (choose, rate, withhold, navigate, play) are Catalog additions, and
only play has a HED tag.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_instructions.md
```

## What the tables do not settle

Whether a facet value should be stored on the task record as the plain value or as its
HED tag string is not yet decided; these tables keep both so that either choice can be
made later without redoing the work. The HED schema version is 8.4.0 throughout, and a schema release that adds a
missing item or action changes the tag column, not the vocabulary.
